structure.title: General disclosures
structure.heading: 1 General disclosures
structure.start_phrase: This sustainability statement (in DNB called sustainability report) has been prepared in accordance with the EU’s Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), which has been implemented in Norwegian law through changes to Section 2-3 of the Norwegian Accounting Act 1, and is based on the associated European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), which have been implemented in Norwegian law in the Regulations relating to standards for sustainability reporting dated 20 December 2024 2.
structure.summary:
- Purpose and framework: The sustainability report (ESRS 2 General disclosures) outlines DNB’s compliance with the EU CSRD and ESRS, as implemented in Norwegian law (Accounting Act amendments and 20 Dec 2024 regulations).
- Reporting scope and boundary: Coverage aligns with the consolidated financial statements for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2024 for the DNB Group (DNB Bank ASA and wholly owned subsidiaries, excluding subsidiaries held for sale). Upstream and downstream value chains are included; downstream reporting is limited to loans, investments, and facilitation through DNB Bank ASA and associated subsidiaries (DNB Asset Management, DNB Livsforsikring, DNB Boligkreditt). Boundaries are set via the double materiality assessment (see ESRS 2 IRO-1).
- Entity-specific disclosures: Certain material topics not fully covered by ESRS—cyber security, financial crime, and financial infrastructure and financial stability—are reported under ESRS S4 and G1. An index indicates fulfilled disclosure requirements, and explanations are provided where requirements are not reported or deemed not material. Phased-in provisions from ESRS 1 Appendix C are applied, and sensitive information on financial infrastructure/stability is omitted per ESRS 1 Section 7.7.
- Changes and estimates: ESRS 2 BP-2 notes that use of estimates for value-chain metrics and changes to greenhouse gas emissions reporting are detailed under ESRS E1 Climate change.
- Governance: Per ESRS 2 GOV-1 and GOV-2, the roles of DNB’s Board of Directors and Group Management in overseeing sustainability ambitions, information flows, and addressed sustainability matters are described.

nodes.title: Basis for preparation

- Clarifies that held-for-sale subsidiaries are excluded from ESRS 2, E1, E3, S1, S4 and G1 disclosures due to their short-term ownership intent.
- Describes value chain coverage: upstream and downstream are included, with downstream limited to loans, investments and facilitation via DNB Bank ASA and key subsidiaries (DNB Asset Management, DNB Livsforsikring, DNB Boligkreditt).
- Notes that value chain boundaries were set through the double materiality assessment and ties to ESRS 2 IRO-1 for process details.
- Identifies entity-specific disclosures for topics not fully covered by ESRS—cybersecurity, financial crime, and financial infrastructure/financial stability—reported under ESRS S4 and ESRS G1.
- States that an index (referenced on page 82) maps which disclosure requirements are met and that explanations are provided where requirements are not reported or deemed not material.
- Confirms use of ESRS 1 phased-in provisions and omission of sensitive information for financial infrastructure/stability per ESRS 1 Section 7.7.
- Indicates that details on estimates for value chain metrics and changes to GHG emissions reporting are provided under ESRS E1 Climate change (ESRS 2 BP-2).
- Outlines governance (ESRS 2 GOV-1 and GOV-2): the Board of Directors and Group Management are responsible for oversight, information flow, and addressing sustainability matters, including management and follow-up of sustainability ambitions.

nodes.heading: 1.2 Changes to sustainability information and use of estimates

nodes.summary:
- Purpose and basis: The sustainability report (sustainability statement) is prepared in line with the EU CSRD and ESRS, as implemented in Norwegian law (Accounting Act §2-3 and Regulations on sustainability reporting dated 20 Dec 2024).
- Reporting scope: Aligns with DNB Group’s consolidated financial statements for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2024, covering DNB Bank ASA and wholly owned subsidiaries (including their underlying subsidiaries), excluding subsidiaries held for sale.
- Exclusions: Subsidiaries held for sale are excluded from sustainability reporting across ESRS 2, E1, E3, S1, S4 and G1 due to short intended ownership duration, though included in financial statements for assumed credit commitments.
- Value chain coverage: Upstream and downstream value chains are included; downstream is limited to loans, investments and facilitation through DNB Bank ASA and associated subsidiaries (DNB Asset Management, DNB Livsforsikring, DNB Boligkreditt).
- Double materiality: The value chain boundaries and material disclosure topics are defined via DNB’s double materiality analysis; further details to be provided under ESRS 2 IRO-1.
- Entity-specific disclosures: Where ESRS do not cover material topics, DNB reports company-specific disclosures—cyber security and financial crime (ESRS S4) and financial infrastructure and financial stability (ESRS G1).
- Reporting completeness: An index (p. 82) shows which disclosure requirements are met; DNB explains any non-reporting or immateriality decisions for impacts, risks and opportunities.
- Phased-in provisions and confidentiality: DNB uses ESRS 1 Appendix C phased-in requirements; sensitive information on financial infrastructure and stability is omitted per ESRS 1 section 7.7.
- Estimates and changes: Information on estimates related to value chain metrics and changes in GHG emissions reporting is provided under ESRS E1 Climate change (ESRS 2 BP-2).
- Governance: Roles and oversight of sustainability by DNB’s Board of Directors and Group Management are addressed under ESRS 2 GOV-1 and GOV-2, including information provided to, and matters addressed by, these bodies.

nodes.title: The role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies
nodes.heading: 1.3.1.1 The role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies
nodes.start_phrase: DNB’s Board of Directors and Group Management team are the Group’s administrative, management and supervisory bodies.
nodes.summary:
- Describes the basis for preparing DNB’s sustainability statement in accordance with the EU CSRD and ESRS, as implemented in Norwegian law (Accounting Act §2-3 and 20 December 2024 ESRS regulations).
- Defines the reporting scope and boundary: aligned with the 2024 consolidated financial statements; covers the DNB Group (DNB Bank ASA and wholly owned subsidiaries and their subsidiaries); excludes subsidiaries held for sale from sustainability reporting (including ESRS 2, E1, E3, S1, S4, G1) due to intended short ownership, though they appear in financials for credit commitment reasons.
- Explains value chain coverage: includes upstream and downstream; downstream limited to loans, investments and facilitation through DNB Bank ASA and related subsidiaries (DNB Asset Management, DNB Livsforsikring, DNB Boligkreditt); boundaries set via the double materiality analysis, with further detail referenced under ESRS 2 IRO-1.
- Notes entity-specific disclosures where ESRS do not fully cover material topics: cyber security, financial crime, and financial infrastructure/financial stability, reported under ESRS S4 and ESRS G1; an index identifies met requirements; explanations are provided for any non-reported or non-material requirements.
- States use of phased-in ESRS 1 Appendix C disclosure provisions and omission of sensitive information on financial infrastructure/financial stability per ESRS 1 Section 7.7.
- Indicates that information on use of estimates for value chain metrics and changes to greenhouse gas emissions reporting is provided under ESRS E1 Climate change.
- Introduces governance context: the Board of Directors and Group Management constitute the administrative, management and supervisory bodies addressing sustainability matters (ESRS 2 GOV-1 and GOV-2).

nodes.title: Information provided to and sustainability matters addressed by the undertaking’s administrative, management and supervisory bodies
nodes.heading: 1.3.1.2 Information provided to and sustainability matters addressed by the undertaking’s administrative, management and supervisory bodies
nodes.start_phrase: DNB’s Board of Directors and Group Management team are the Group’s administrative, management and supervisory bodies.
nodes.summary:
- Basis and scope: The sustainability report (sustainability statement) is prepared in accordance with the EU CSRD and ESRS, as implemented in Norwegian law. It covers the DNB Group’s consolidated reporting period 1 January–31 December 2024, including DNB Bank ASA and wholly owned subsidiaries (excluding subsidiaries held for sale), and includes upstream and downstream value chains; downstream coverage is limited to loans, investments and facilitation through DNB Bank ASA and associated subsidiaries (DNB Asset Management, DNB Livsforsikring, DNB Boligkreditt).
- Materiality and reporting boundaries: The value chain boundary is defined through DNB’s double materiality analysis (ESRS 2 IRO-1). Some disclosure requirements are entity-specific where ESRS does not fully cover material topics (cyber security, financial crime, financial infrastructure and financial stability, reported under ESRS S4 and G1). DNB applies phased‑in ESRS 1 provisions (Appendix C) and omits sensitive information on financial infrastructure and stability per ESRS 1 section 7.7. Where requirements are not reported, explanations are provided; an index (p. 82) maps disclosures to material topics.
- Estimates and methodology changes: Information on use of estimates for value chain metrics and changes to GHG emissions reporting is addressed under ESRS E1 Climate change.
- Governance structure and oversight (ESRS 2 GOV-1, GOV-2): 
  - Board of Directors: Holds ultimate responsibility for sound organisation and strategy, sets sustainability ambitions, transition plan, and sustainable financing targets, and establishes conduct expectations via the Code of Conduct. Audit Committee oversees sustainability reporting and internal control; Risk Management Committee oversees risk management. The Board signs the sustainability report and the Norwegian Transparency Act report. In 2024, it reviewed the double materiality analysis, regularly discussed climate transition and transition plan implementation, monitored progress on climate, diversity/equality, and financial crime metrics, and received quarterly risk updates. The Board and Audit Committee received CSRD training. Composition highlights: no executives on the Board, 50/50 gender split, three employee representatives, and 63% independent members.
  - CEO and Group Management: The CEO is responsible for executing strategy and performance, including sustainability, and signs the sustainability and Transparency Act reports. The Group Management team (CEO and Group EVPs) reviews financials and risk appetite monthly and regularly addresses ESG matters, including CSRD implementation in 2024. They drive and track the transition plan; each unit reports progress. The EVP Risk Management develops risk culture, ensures regulatory compliance, and provides quarterly risk reports.
  - Sustainability division in Group Finance: Central function for strategic and operational sustainability work, covering sustainability ambitions, transition plan, and sustainable financing targets; advises management and business areas. The division’s EVP reports under the CFO; the CFO informs the CEO on significant issues.
- Risk management, controls and procedures: Impacts, risks and opportunities are managed through corporate governance, the double materiality process, and a defined risk appetite that includes non‑financial risks. Sustainability risk is integrated into risk assessments and monitored with recovery plan indicators. Regulatory compliance processes are in place. Employees receive training on relevant sustainability risks (e.g., data protection, anti‑corruption) via Motimate. Clear upward reporting lines ensure timely communication to management and the Board through risk and performance reporting, with the CEO updating the Board on significant matters. Internal control follows the three lines of defence; Group Audit (third line) provides independent assurance and advisory to strengthen risk management, internal control, and governance.

nodes.title: Incentive schemes
nodes.heading: 1.3.2 Incentive schemes
nodes.start_phrase: DNB’s guidelines for determining remuneration to the CEO and other members of the Group Management team should, at all times, support the Group’s current strategy and values, while contributing to the attainment of the Group’s targets.
nodes.summary:
- Focus: ESRS 2 GOV-3 on integrating sustainability-related performance into incentive schemes at DNB.
- Governance: The Board prepares remuneration guidelines for executive and non-executive directors; the Annual General Meeting approves at least every four years or upon significant changes. The Board sets the CEO’s variable remuneration; the CEO sets variable remuneration for other Group Management members.
- CEO variable pay structure: 60% based on a single financial performance criterion; 40% based on five strategy and sustainability criteria (8% each).
- Sustainability/strategic criteria and measurement:
  - Sustainable transition (8%): qualitative assessment against DNB’s role in driving sustainable transition and progress on the Group’s transition plan; no annual targets and non-linear progress, assessed against long-term objectives.
  - Stable and secure IT operations (8%): quantitative, measured by the number of serious IT operational incidents; underpins competitiveness and a safe digital economy.
  - Engagement and diversity (8%): qualitative, based on employee surveys, gender balance in management, and DNB’s societal position on diversity and equality.
  - Compliance (8%): qualitative, focused on reducing compliance risk, informed by internal control and government assessments.
  - Reputation and customer satisfaction (8%): qualitative, based on changes in reputation and overall customer satisfaction across segments.
- Group Management team scorecard: Emphasizes the Board’s evaluation by weighting the Group-wide scorecard at a minimum of 50% for all eligible members; remaining targets combine financial and strategic criteria tied to each EVP’s area of responsibility.
- Scorecard components: Group-wide financial/strategic targets, financial unit targets, strategic unit targets (covering the same five themes as above), and individual targets. Individual targets generally account for 15% (most units) and 20% for Group units.

nodes.title: Integration of sustainability-related performance in incentive schemes
nodes.heading: 1.3.2.1 Integration of sustainability-related performance in incentive schemes
nodes.start_phrase: DNB’s guidelines for determining remuneration to the CEO and other members of the Group Management team should, at all times, support the Group’s current strategy and values, while contributing to the attainment of the Group’s targets.
nodes.summary:
The fragment describes DNB’s incentive schemes under ESRS 2 GOV-3, showing how sustainability-related performance is integrated into executive remuneration.

- Governance and approval: The Board prepares remuneration guidelines for executive and non-executive directors; the Annual General Meeting approves these at least every four years or upon significant change. The Board sets the CEO’s variable remuneration in line with the approved guidelines; the CEO sets variable pay for other Group Management members.

- CEO variable remuneration structure: 
  - 60% based on a single financial performance criterion.
  - 40% based on five strategy and sustainability criteria (8% each):
    - Sustainable transition: qualitative assessment of DNB’s role in driving sustainable transition and progress on the Group’s transition plan (no fixed annual, linear targets; Board judges satisfactory progress vs long-term goals).
    - Stable and secure IT operations: quantitative measure based on the number of serious IT incidents, supporting a safe digital economy.
    - Engagement and diversity: qualitative assessment using employee surveys, management gender balance, and societal standing on diversity and equality.
    - Compliance: qualitative assessment of compliance risk reduction, informed by internal control and regulatory evaluations.
    - Reputation and customer satisfaction: qualitative assessment of reputation trends and overall customer satisfaction across segments.

- Variable remuneration for other Group Management:
  - Scorecard-based approach that gives significant weight (minimum 50%) to the Group-wide scorecard so Board evaluation of Group target attainment is emphasized for all bonus-eligible members.
  - Remaining weight combines:
    - Unit-level financial targets (where applicable).
    - Unit-level strategic targets aligned to the five strategic/sustainability areas above.
    - Individual performance, reflecting the unit’s dashboard and contribution to Group value creation.
  - Weights vary by role (e.g., CFO, Technology & Services, Business areas, Group units), as detailed in an internal table.

Overall, the section evidences clear integration of sustainability, operational resilience, compliance, and stakeholder outcomes into executive incentives alongside financial performance.

nodes.title: Statement on due diligence
nodes.heading: 1.3.3.1 Statement on due diligence
nodes.start_phrase: The table below contains an overview of where information has been given about the Group’s process for due diligence in this sustainability report.
nodes.summary:
- Provides an overview of where the DNB Group discloses its due diligence process in the sustainability report, aligned with ESRS 2 GOV-4.
- Maps the five core elements of due diligence to specific ESRS sections and pages:
  - Embedding due diligence in governance, strategy, and business model: ESRS 2 GOV-2 (p. 63), GOV-3 (p. 65), SBM-3 with topical standards E1 Climate, E3 Water, S1 Own workforce, S4 Consumers and end-users, G1 Business conduct (various pages).
  - Stakeholder engagement across all due diligence steps: ESRS 2 GOV-2 (p. 62), SBM-2 (p. 72), IRO-1 (p. 76), MDR-P with topical standards (e.g., E1 p. 112; S1 p. 135; G1 p. 167).
  - Identifying and assessing adverse impacts: ESRS 2 IRO-1 (p. 76), SBM-3 (p. 75) with topical standards (e.g., E1 p. 108; E3 p. 131; S1 p. 134; S4 pp. 140/145/150; G1 pp. 156/160/163/167), and SBM-1 (p. 67).
  - Actions to address adverse impacts: ESRS 2 MDR-A with topical standards (e.g., E1 p. 113; E3 p. 132; S1 p. 137; S4 pp. 142/147/151; G1 pp. 158/161/164/168), and SBM-1 (p. 67).
  - Tracking effectiveness and communicating: ESRS 2 MDR-T and MDR-M with topical standards (e.g., E1 p. 117; S1 p. 138; S4 pp. 144/149/152; G1 pp. 158/162/165/169).
- Describes risk management and internal controls over sustainability reporting (ESRS 2 GOV-5):
  - Implementation of an internal control system based on the COSO framework, with key controls to reduce reporting errors and ongoing monitoring.
  - Internal Control over Sustainability Reporting (ICSR) instructions set group-wide principles and apply to all DNB Group entities in scope.
  - Annual, risk-based assessments to identify areas with potential for significant reporting errors; yearly status reporting to the Audit Committee and Group Management.
  - Defined risk types include immature disclosure processes, reliance on estimates and forward-looking assumptions, third-party information risks, and incentives that could lead to misreporting.

nodes.title: Risk management and internal control in the sustainability reporting
nodes.heading: 1.3.4 Risk management and internal control in the sustainability reporting
nodes.start_phrase: The Group is working to implement an internal control system for sustainability reporting based on the principles in the framework from the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).
nodes.summary:
- Presents ESRS 2 GOV-4 Statement on due diligence, mapping where each core due-diligence element is disclosed across the sustainability report with page references:
  - Embedding due diligence in governance, strategy, and business model (GOV-2, GOV-3, SBM-3) with topical ESRS references: E1 Climate change, E3 Water and marine resources, S1 Own workforce, S4 Consumers and end-users, G1 Business conduct.
  - Engaging with affected stakeholders across all due-diligence steps (GOV-2, SBM-2, IRO-1, MDR-P) with topical links to E1, S1, and G1.
  - Identifying and assessing adverse impacts (IRO-1, SBM-3 with topical ESRS; SBM-1).
  - Taking actions to address adverse impacts (MDR-A with topical ESRS; SBM-1).
  - Tracking effectiveness and communicating (MDR-T and MDR-M with topical ESRS), all accompanied by specific page numbers.

- Details ESRS 2 GOV-5 on risk management and internal controls over sustainability reporting:
  - Implementation of a COSO-based Internal Control over Sustainability Reporting (ICSR) framework with key controls to reduce reporting errors and ongoing follow-up.
  - Group-wide applicability to all DNB entities covered by the sustainability report.
  - Annual reporting of internal control status to the Audit Committee and Group Management.
  - Risk-based approach with annual risk assessments to identify areas with potential for significant reporting errors.
  - Defined risk types: immature disclosure processes; reliance on estimates, expectations, and forward-looking assumptions; third-party information risks; and incentives to report incorrect information.

nodes.title: Risk management and internal controls over sustainability reporting
nodes.heading: 1.3.4.1 Risk management and internal controls over sustainability reporting
nodes.start_phrase: The Group is working to implement an internal control system for sustainability reporting based on the principles in the framework from the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).
nodes.summary:
- Outlines DNB’s due diligence approach under ESRS 2 GOV-4, providing a roadmap to where each core element is covered in the sustainability report:
  - Embedding due diligence in governance, strategy, and the business model.
  - Stakeholder engagement across key steps.
  - Identification and assessment of adverse impacts.
  - Actions to address adverse impacts.
  - Tracking effectiveness and communicating outcomes.
  - Cross-references span ESRS topic standards for climate (E1), water (E3), own workforce (S1), consumers/end-users (S4), and business conduct/financial stability (G1).

- Describes risk management and internal control over sustainability reporting (ESRS 2 GOV-5):
  - Implementation of an Internal Control over Sustainability Reporting (ICSR) system based on the COSO framework, with key controls and follow-up.
  - Risk-based approach with annual risk assessments to prevent material errors, focusing on immature disclosure processes, estimates/assumptions, third-party information, and incentives to misreport.
  - Use of materiality thresholds to determine coverage; mitigation measures include standardized processes, guidelines, procedures, and enhanced IT systems/tools.
  - Governance and oversight mirror financial reporting: Board Audit Committee oversight; Group EVPs as risk owners; Group Finance defines ICSR scope; external auditor provides assurance and findings are followed up by management.

- Summarizes strategy, business model, and value chain (ESRS 2 SBM-1):
  - DNB is Norway’s largest financial institution, serving 2.4 million personal and 236,000 corporate customers with broad financial services.
  - Predominantly Norwegian market with strong Nordic and international presence across sectors such as energy, seafood, shipping, health, technology, and telecom; about one-fifth of income from international operations.
  - Active financing of renewable energy projects, particularly internationally; 19-country footprint with new 2024 representative offices in Australia (corporate/renewables) and Switzerland (personal).
  - Workforce of 11,515 employees distributed across Norway, Europe, the Americas, Asia and Oceania.
  - Greatest sustainability impacts, risks, and opportunities arise downstream through lending and investments; direct impacts include own workforce, business ethics, and combating financial crime.
  - Sustainability is integrated into Group strategy with an ambition for sustainable value creation and to drive the sustainable transition.

- ICSR approach: Materiality thresholds set disclosure scope based on identified risk, with key risks tied to estimates and immature information processes. Norway is the main market with significant Nordic and international operations (~20% of income), including financing for renewable energy. Presence in 19 countries; 2024 openings in Australia (corporate/renewables) and Switzerland (personal). Workforce of 11,515, mainly in Norway, with noted geographic distribution.

nodes.title: Products and services within sustainable finance
nodes.heading: 1.4.1.2 Products and services within sustainable finance
nodes.start_phrase: DNB offers several products and services within sustainable finance, including loans for increasing energy efficiency in homes, sustainability-linked loans to corporate customers and mutual funds with a sustainability profile 6.
nodes.summary:
- DNB’s sustainability ambitions: finance the climate transition and drive sustainable value creation; promote diversity and inclusion; combat financial crime and support a secure digital economy.
- 2023 transition plan: strategy to reduce both financed and own emissions and promote sustainable development via products and services; sectoral targets for oil and gas, shipping, and commercial property; focus on supporting customers while reducing portfolio climate risk; current limitations on ESRS E1-1 disclosures.
- Sustainable finance frameworks: a loan portfolio framework aligned with LMA Green Loan and Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles, EU Taxonomy, and developed with Sustainalytics; 2024 launch of a third‑party‑verified transition loan framework.
- Product suite: green guarantees; sustainability‑linked loans; green loans; renewable energy financing; environmentally friendly transport financing; sustainable bonds; advisory on debt, equity and M&A; green mortgages, home equity credit lines, construction loans, fixed‑rate loans and holiday home loans; environmental loans; and mutual funds with a sustainability profile (SFDR Articles 8/9).
- Sustainability risk management in credit and investments: integration of sustainability risk in credit decisions; mandatory commentary above NOK 8 million and detailed ESG risk classification above NOK 50 million using an in‑house tool; DNB Asset Management assesses ESG risks/opportunities and avoids unethical or unsustainable activities.
- Financing targets: mobilise NOK 1,500 billion for the sustainable transition by 2030; additional 2025 targets for sustainability‑profiled mutual funds; products primarily climate‑related but can address biodiversity and resource efficiency; emphasis on product integrity and advisory competence.
- Product assessment (2023): review against GFANZ net‑zero product guidance indicates offerings align with best practices and support customer transition; varying product maturity (notably sustainability‑linked financing); ongoing expert‑led improvements; rapid monitoring of evolving regulation and market expectations; data access and quality remain key challenges, with efforts to enhance climate data collection/structuring.
- Advisory services: growing importance of transition‑oriented advice and competence sharing; provision of green guarantees and derivatives linked to green loans and bonds.
- Net‑zero commitment: target of net‑zero emissions in lending and investment portfolios by 2050; partnership and engagement over divestment as the primary approach; financing may be withheld from companies unwilling to transition; success depends on supportive policy frameworks and stakeholder collaboration.
- Value chain overview: upstream (capital raising and procurement of IT, consulting, property/office services); own operations (employees, energy use, governance and compliance); downstream (customer products and services including lending, facilitation and investment).

nodes.title: DNB's value chain

- Strategic objectives: deliver profitable, stable performance to secure capital for climate transition financing, anti-financial-crime efforts, talent attraction/retention, and customer-centric innovation.
- Stakeholder dialogue (ESRS 2 SBM-2): commitment to open engagement on environmental, social, and governance topics; identification and integration of stakeholder perspectives into decision-making and strategic planning; definition of stakeholders as those influenced by or able to influence DNB’s operations, products, and services.

nodes.title: Material impacts, risks and opportunities
nodes.heading: 1.6 Material impacts, risks and opportunities
nodes.start_phrase: DNB has carried out a double materiality analysis in accordance with the principles and requirements in the ESRS.
nodes.summary:
- Overview: The section summarizes DNB’s ESRS 2 SBM-3 disclosure on material impacts, risks, and opportunities, based on a double materiality analysis conducted in line with ESRS (with process details under ESRS 2 IRO-1).

- Material topics identified:
  - ESRS E1 Climate change
  - ESRS E3 Water and marine resources
  - ESRS S1 Own workforce
  - ESRS S4 Consumers and end-users
  - ESRS G1 Business conduct
  - Company-specific topics reported under S4/G1: cyber security, financial crime, and financial infrastructure & financial stability
  - Other ESRS topics were considered but fell below the materiality threshold this year.

- Key impacts, risks, and opportunities by topic:
  - Climate (E1): Indirect negative impacts via financed and invested activities; exposure to transition risk (policy/market shifts) and physical climate risk (extreme weather). Opportunities arise from financing clients’ transition to more sustainable business models.
  - Water and marine resources (E3): Significant due to DNB’s large seafood portfolio; need for responsible marine resource management to reduce ecosystem harm and protect DNB from credit risk (e.g., potential loan defaults if clients’ revenues decline).
  - Own workforce (S1): Potential for positive impact as a large employer through diversity and gender equality initiatives.
  - Consumers and end-users (S4): Material impacts and financial risks tied to personal data management, customer advice and guidance, and cyber-attack prevention; customer care is central to value creation.
  - Business conduct (G1): Corruption and bribery, corporate culture, financial crime, and financial stability/infrastructure are material due to financial risk and broader impacts on customers and society if not effectively managed.

- Integration and scope:
  - Impacts, risks, and opportunities are linked to different parts of DNB’s business model and value chain.

- Purpose and scope: Discloses DNB’s ESRS 2 SBM-3 and IRO-1 outcomes, detailing a double materiality analysis and how material impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) interact with strategy and the business model.
- Material topics identified:

  - ESRS E3 Water and marine resources: Material due to significant seafood exposure; need for responsible marine resource management to limit ecosystem/biodiversity harm and reduce credit risk from potential client income loss; primarily downstream.
  - ESRS S1 Own workforce: Diversity, gender equality and equal pay material in own operations; potential for positive impacts as a major employer.
  - ESRS S4 Consumers and end-users: Data privacy, access to quality information, advice/guidance, and cyber security are material; direct impact on customers/end-users and related financial risk; primarily downstream.
  - ESRS G1 Business conduct: Corporate culture, corruption and bribery are material in own operations; company-specific topics—financial crime and financial infrastructure/stability—also material due to financial and societal risks.

nodes.title: Description of the processes to identify and assess material impacts, risks and opportunities
nodes.heading: 1.7.1.1 Description of the processes to identify and assess material impacts, risks and opportunities
nodes.start_phrase: A double materiality analysis is prepared to identify and rank DNB’s impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) in environmental, social and corporate governance-related matters in the value chain.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines DNB’s 2024 double materiality analysis under CSRD and ESRS 1–2, detailing how the Group identifies, assesses, and governs material impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs) across its value chain. It presents a topic matrix showing positive/negative impacts, risks, opportunities, time horizons (short, medium, long), and value-chain location. Material topics include:
- E1 Climate change (adaptation, mitigation, energy) – mainly downstream.
- E3 Water and marine resources (extraction/use of marine resources) – downstream.
- S1 Own workforce (diversity; gender equality and equal pay) – own operations.
- S4 Consumers/end-users (privacy/data protection; access to quality information; cybersecurity as a company-specific topic) – downstream.
- G1 Business conduct (corporate culture; corruption and bribery; financial crime and financial infrastructure/stability as company-specific topics) – own operations.

DNB integrates IRO monitoring into strategy and risk management, with annual Group-wide risk assessments and Pillar 3 reporting, aligned with CRD/CRR. The materiality process follows EFRAG’s 2024 guidance: 
- Step 1 maps scope, value chain, and stakeholders (employees, suppliers/partners, society/authorities, customers, investors/owners, internal experts). The value chain is delimited to loans, investments, and investment services; assessment generally stops at direct relationships, except for financed GHG emissions (Scope 3) and human rights, which extend further. DNB’s exposure is largely Norwegian across sectors like oil and gas, shipping, real estate, and seafood.
- Step 2 identifies IROs using ESRS AR16, UNEP FI’s Portfolio Impact Analysis Tool, a 10% exposure threshold, qualitative assessments for S1 and G1, company-specific topics, and dependency considerations.
- Step 3 assesses IROs over S/M/L horizons using qualitative severity (scale, scope, irremediability) and likelihood scales; human-rights likelihood is set at 100%. A threshold of 4+ prioritizes topics. Results are aggregated with higher weight on the loan portfolio.
- Step 4 secures management and Board approval.

Topic-specific methods include scenario analyses for climate (NGFS, CRREM, SBTi), finding transition risk exceeds physical risk; qualitative sector-based assessments for pollution, water/marine, biodiversity (with exclusions for protected areas; below threshold in 2024), and circular economy. The outcome confirms material IROs in E1, E3, S1, S4, and G1 (plus company-specific topics), with ongoing enhancements to policies and plans and further strategy/action plan development in 2025. An index maps ESRS 2 disclosure requirements to identified IROs.

nodes.title: Indices

- Outlines weighting and assessment aligned with ESRS 1 Sections 3.4 and 3.5, using 1–5 qualitative scales for severity of negative impacts (scale, scope, irremediable character) and a 0–100% likelihood scale; sets likelihood of potential negative human rights impacts at 100% per ESRS 1. Positive impacts use analogous scale/scope/likelihood measures.
- Notes that financial effects of risks and opportunities could not be quantified during the reporting year; therefore, qualitative severity and likelihood assessments were applied, with severity tied to potential loss of benefit to DNB.
- Establishes a prioritization threshold of 4 (or higher) for material topics, calibrated to existing risk frameworks and climate risk tolerance; Group Risk Management and internal experts were consulted to set the threshold.
- Explains separate analyses for loan/facilitation operations and the investment portfolio, then aggregated at Group level with higher weighting to the loan portfolio due to its larger size, greater impact and financial exposure, and DNB’s direct credit risk versus DAM’s minority shareholdings.
- Step 4 details governance and internal control: ongoing support from internal stakeholders, with Group Management and Board involvement and approval of the material topics.
- Reports that material IROs fall under ESRS topical standards E1, E3, S1, S4, and G1, plus company-specific topics under S4 and G1; existing policies and goals cover several areas, while newly identified topics will require strategies, action plans, and objectives to be developed in 2025.
- Presents an ESRS 2 IRO-2 index of disclosure requirements: tables list all ESRS 2 and applicable topical disclosures, including company-specific ones; applicability is based on the double materiality analysis, phasing-in rules, and EFRAG memo ID 177, with guidance for navigating the sustainability report and comments on non-applicable disclosures.

nodes.start_phrase: The tables below show all of the ESRS disclosure requirements in ESRS 2 and the applicable disclosure requirements in the topical standards, in addition to disclosure requirements for the company-specific topics.
nodes.summary:
- Explains Step 3 of DNB’s double materiality process: assessing identified impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) across short (0–1 year), medium (2–5 years) and long-term (>5 years) horizons, noting several topics span all horizons, and weighting in line with ESRS 1 Sections 3.4–3.5.
